prompt: Looking toward the limb of the Sun, you see higher, cooler layers than at disc centre. Why?
options: Light at the limb is scattered more strongly by dust, which lowers the temperature seen
An oblique line of sight reaches optical depth 1 at higher altitude
The Sun is cooler at the limb than at the centre of the disc
The limb is closer to the observer than the centre
answer: An oblique line of sight reaches optical depth 1 at higher altitude
explanation: The optical-depth path length scales as 1/μ, so you sample shallower layers.
hint: Compare path lengths at different angles.

prompt: In the Eddington grey relation, find T/Teff at optical depth 2/3.
explanation: The grey relation is (T/Teff)⁴ = (3/4)(τ + 2/3). At τ = 2/3 the bracket is 4/3, so the factor is 1 and T/Teff = 1.
